adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:139 — Deleted `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` with no replacement test verifying the new silent-overwrite-on-duplicate-group-key behavior in `process_detectors`/`evaluate`'s dict-based results

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the duplicate-group-key detection/logging in `process_detectors` (the `detector_group_keys` set and the `logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found")` block) and changes `evaluate` to return a `dict` that is built via `results[result.group_key] = result`, which will silently overwrite on key collision. The test `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` that previously asserted this duplicate-key path/logging is deleted and no new test asserts the new (overwrite/no-log) behavior or otherwise guards against accidental key collisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:289 — result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence` is an annotation-only statement with no assignment, immediately followed by conditional assignment; confusing/dead statement that misleads readers into thinking a value was set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an annotation-only statement (`result: StatusChangeMessage | IssueOccurrence`) without assignment in `evaluate_group_key_value`, but it’s not a functional defect: both branches of the subsequent `if new_status == ...` assign `result` before it’s used in the returned `DetectorEvaluationResult`. The finding is essentially a readability/style nit rather than a verifiable bug or substantial review issue grounded in behavior.
